```{r setup, include=FALSE}
#table 1

library(gt)
library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
table1_inclusion <- all_results %>%
  mutate(
    truth = ifelse(variable %in% true_vars, "TRUE", "FALSE")
  ) %>%
  group_by(method, n, rho, truth, sim_id) %>%
  summarize(
    n_selected = sum(selected),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  group_by(method, n, rho, truth) %>%
  summarize(
    percent_selected = mean(n_selected > 0) * 100,
    mean_selected = mean(n_selected),
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  pivot_longer(
    cols = c(percent_selected, mean_selected),
    names_to = "summary",
    values_to = "value"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    summary = recode(
      summary,
      percent_selected = "% > 0 selected",
      mean_selected = "Mean # selected"
    ),
    setting = paste0("N=", n, ", rho=", rho, ", ", truth)
  ) %>%
  select(method, summary, setting, value) %>%
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = setting,
    values_from = value
  )

table1_inclusion %>%
  gt(rowname_col = "summary", groupname_col = "method") %>%
  
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table 1. Inclusion of Truly and Falsely Associated Variables**"),
    subtitle = "Percent of simulations selecting variables and average number selected"
  ) %>%
  
  fmt_number(
    columns = where(is.numeric),
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  
  cols_label(
    method = "Method"
  ) %>%
  
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = 12,
    heading.title.font.size = 14,
    heading.subtitle.font.size = 11,
    data_row.padding = px(4)
  )
```

## R Markdown

This is an R Markdown document. Markdown is a simple formatting syntax for authoring HTML, PDF, and MS Word documents. For more details on using R Markdown see <http://rmarkdown.rstudio.com>.

When you click the **Knit** button a document will be generated that includes both content as well as the output of any embedded R code chunks within the document. You can embed an R code chunk like this:

```{r cars}
#table 2
table2_true_vars <- all_results %>%
  filter(variable %in% true_vars) %>%
  group_by(method, n, rho, variable, beta_true) %>%
  summarize(
    selection_percent = mean(selected) * 100,
    bias = mean(bias_uncond, na.rm = TRUE),
    coverage_percent = mean(covered, na.rm = TRUE) * 100,
    .groups = "drop"
  ) %>%
  mutate(
    Beta = round(beta_true, 2),
    setting = paste0("N=", n, ", rho=", rho)
  ) %>%
  select(
    method,
    variable,
    Beta,
    setting,
    selection_percent,
    bias,
    coverage_percent
  )

table2_true_vars %>%
  gt(groupname_col = "method") %>%
  
  tab_header(
    title = md("**Table 2. Selection Frequency, Bias, and Coverage for Truly Associated Variables**"),
    subtitle = "Results for variables X1 through X5"
  ) %>%
  
  tab_spanner(
    label = "Performance Measures",
    columns = c(selection_percent, bias, coverage_percent)
  ) %>%
  
  cols_label(
    variable = "Variable",
    Beta = "True Beta",
    setting = "Simulation Setting",
    selection_percent = "Selection %",
    bias = "Bias",
    coverage_percent = "Coverage %"
  ) %>%
  
  fmt_number(
    columns = c(selection_percent, coverage_percent),
    decimals = 1
  ) %>%
  
  fmt_number(
    columns = bias,
    decimals = 2
  ) %>%
  
  tab_options(
    table.font.size = 12,
    heading.title.font.size = 14,
    heading.subtitle.font.size = 11,
    data_row.padding = px(4)
  )
```

## Including Plots

You can also embed plots, for example:

```{r pressure, echo=FALSE}
plot(pressure)
```

Note that the `echo = FALSE` parameter was added to the code chunk to prevent printing of the R code that generated the plot.
